name: Byzantine Reconquest of Eastern Frontier
summary: Byzantine Emperor Nicephorus II Phocas retakes Aleppo and much of Cilicia, reversing centuries of Arab expansion. His campaigns, followed by those of John Tzimiskes and Basil II, temporarily extend Byzantine borders to Syria and parts of the Holy Land. The campaigns demonstrate a militarily resurgent Byzantium that contemporaries describe as a renewed Roman empire.

_quarry.structural_significance: Byzantine expansion into Syria and the Holy Land revives the political geography of the ancient Roman Empire; the reconquest of Antioch inspires the crusading idea of recovering Christian holy sites.
